title: Mobartech, an informal education project for bringing people closer to cultural heritage
extended_summary:
This paper describes the MOBARTECH project, an informal education and cultural heritage initiative aimed at engaging the public in the study, conservation, and interpretation of heritage assets. The author frames the work as a response to the need for more participatory, learner-centered approaches to heritage education, especially in contexts where cultural sites are poorly understood by local residents and visitors.

The intervention was developed around the UNESCO World Heritage site of Mantua and Sabbioneta in Italy. The project combined questionnaires, interviews with key informants, observations, archival research, and collaborative work with secondary school students to design a guided-discovery kit for visitors. The kit incorporated hands-on and digitally supported activities such as observation, drawing, writing, maps, photographs, and downloadable videos.

Participants included local and tourist respondents, community members, and groups of middle and high school students, some of whom were on educational work placements or field trips. The paper reports that involving students in the kit-development process encouraged critical thinking about local heritage and helped them identify meaningful information for communication to others. The main conclusion is that direct participation, co-construction of knowledge, and active engagement can strengthen cultural awareness and heritage appreciation; however, the paper does not provide rigorous comparative evidence of learning gains or any science-achievement outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/descriptive conference paper with no rigorous experimental or quasi-experimental evaluation of an AI or educational technology intervention. It does not provide a controlled design, outcome statistics, or causal evidence relevant to K-12 science learning.
impact_tier_rationale: No measurable impact on science achievement, reasoning, vocabulary, inquiry skills, retention, engagement, or assignment performance is reported. The paper is about cultural heritage informal education, so it shows no direct evidence of impact for Khanmigo or K-12 science learning.

finding.finding_summary: This is an informal education/cultural heritage project, not a Khanmigo or other AI-tutoring study. The paper describes a participatory community project that aimed to increase public engagement with heritage and strengthen links between local communities, schools, and the UNESCO site; however, it reports no quantitative learning gains or causal comparison against standard instruction. Evidence is descriptive and process-oriented, centered on pilot testing and iterative refinement of a guided discovery kit rather than measured achievement outcomes.
finding.measure: Questionnaires, interviews, observations, pilot testing of a guided discovery kit, and qualitative documentation of project phases
